messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and German characters
messages.body_plain:
The key is to know the character encoding of your Rnw file, and you
have to pass that encoding to knitr::knit(). If it is really UTF8
encoded, you may call

library(knitr)
knit('input.Rnw', encoding='UTF-8')

And you have to use \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} in the LaTeX preamble.
Then you compile input.tex with whatever LaTeX tools you want. You did
not send an example, so it is impossible to know what was going on.
Your actual encoding might be iso-8859-15, in which case you use
\usepackage[latin9]{inputenc} and knit('input.Rnw',
encoding='iso-8859-15').

I recommend you to try RStudio instead, which handles encoding
automatically so you do not need to type all these knit() commands.
However, you still need to be aware of the encoding, since you have to
decide \usepackage[???]{inputenc}.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

On Sat, Feb 15, 2014 at 1:07 PM, Thell Fowler <tbfo...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Examples from the xtable gallery done using markdown.
>
> http://rpubs.com/Thell/xtable
>
> Most of the tables in the xtable gallery work great with the
> toMathJax.xtable() function that is a slightly modified toLatex.xtable()
> function.  The stuff you'd normally do with xtable (sanitizing, inserts at
> rows, row and column name control etc. can be done the same way as usual.
>
> Implements:
>
> Output hooks to wrap xtable latex with $$
> Output hook handles 'holding' with a holdjax=TRUE option
> Implements opts.label groups for "jax" "jaxhold" and "jaxasis"
>
>
> The chunks look clean.
>
> For example:
>
> ```{r, opts.label="jax"}
> ## Demonstrate sanitization
> mat <- round(matrix(c(0.9, 0.89, 200, 0.045, 2.0), c(1, 5)), 4)
> rownames(mat) <- "y_{t-1}"
> colnames(mat) <- c("R^2", "\\bar{R}^2", "F-stat", "S.E.E", "DW")
> toMathJax.xtable( xtable(mat), sanitize.text.function=function(x){x})
> ```
>
> Gives just what you'd expect for Latex col/row names.
>
> And inserting chunk output into math sections is pretty straight forward
> too.
>
> $$
> \begin{equation}
> f(x) = \left[ \hspace2ex
> ```{r, opts.label="jaxasis"}
> toMathJax.xtable( xtable( matrix( 1:9, 3, 3) ),
>                   include.rownames=FALSE,
>                   include.colnames=FALSE )
> ```
> \hspace2ex \right]
> \end{equation}
> $$
>
> A feature request has been made to xtable to allow control of the first
> \hline.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and cloud
messages.body_plain:
One solution is to separate the computation from the presentation. Put your computations in an R file, run them at the computing facility of your choice to generate result objects in memory, and save.image to store them. Move the RData file to your workstation and just load the RData file in your Rmd/Rnw file and generate presentable results.

stargazer(model, type="html", summary=F)
```

The stargazer code works fine if the xtable chunk is removed.

Any ideas?

messages.body_plain:
The perl code in my knitr/R script that runs the external tool called bowtie2:

...
....
...
```{r test-perl, engine='perl'}
use strict;
use warnings;
use Cwd qw(cwd);
my $cur_dir = cwd;
print "\nCurrent working dir: [$cur_dir]\n\n";
my $bowtie2_exe = '/data/installs/bowtie2/bowtie2-2.2.1/bowtie2';
...
...
my $cmd="$bowtie2_exe -x $bowtie2_index -1 $fastq_file_pe_1 -2 $fastq_file_pe_2 -S $cur_dir/"."$fastq_files[$cnt]".".sam -p 8";
print "\ncommand is [$cmd]\n";
system($cmd);
...
...

The variables are populated earlier in the code.  The translated command as reported in the knitr report text file is:

## command is [/data/installs/bowtie2/bowtie2-2.2.1/bowtie2 -x /data/ref_genomes/human/37.2/Homo_sapiens/NCBI/build37.2/Sequence/Bowtie2Index/genome -1 /data/projects/knitr/xxxx_1.clipped.fastq.gz -2 /data/projects/knitr/xxxx_2.clipped.fastq.gz -S /data/projects/knitr/xxxx.sam -p 8]

When the command is done running, the output from the command is printed out in the R console:

53545457 reads; of these:
  53545457 (100.00%) were paired; of these:
    6637517 (12.40%) aligned concordantly 0 times
...
...

But this is not captured in the knitr report text file.

Ideally it is important to capture this because a change in the parameters to the bowtie2 command will generate a different output, which should be captured in the report.  Otherwise I would have to copy and paste it in the report.

Please let me know if you need further information.

Thanks,

- Pankaj

messages.subject: Using child documents with RMarkdown V2
messages.subject_clean: Using child documents with RMarkdown V2
messages.body_plain:
In the past I have made heavy use of child documents with knitr both with *.Rmd and *.Rnw files.  I am using RMarkdown V2 (RStudio Version 0.98.737) and the 'knit html' in RStudio works as expected.  When I use the new 'knit PDF' in RStudio with a *.Rmd child document that includes graphs....none of the graphs appear in the final pdf.  What am I missing?  Or is this something I should not be attempting...ie use .Rnw if I want *.pdf output?

Here is a basic example:

---
title: "New Stuff!"
author: "Clueless"
date: "March 30, 2014"
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document:
    highlight: tango
    keep_tex: yes
  word_document: default
geometry: margin=1in
fontsize: 12pt
---

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r comment = NA}
summary(cars)
```

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
plot(cars)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r comment = NA, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x = cut, y = price)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
```

```{r child='./Children/child1.Rmd'}
```

The child document follows...which is stored in a folder named Children

---
title: "child1"
author: "Clueless"
date: "March 30, 2014"
output: html_document
---

This is child 1.

```{r Rhist, fig.align = "center"}
hist(rnorm(1000), col = "red")
```

Here is some *ggplot2*

```{r GRAPHS, fig.align='center', warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x = carat, y = price)) + geom_point(alpha = .2) + theme_bw()
```

The document compiles but does not include graphs (the pdf version)...

TIA for any pointers!

Alan-

The larger problem is I am trying to update my class notes to pdf...using a parent.Rmd that makes several calls to children.Rmd documents...
The notes are on

https://github.com/alanarnholt/STT3850/blob/master/Notes/Parent/Parent.Rmd
